correctness.rationale: The proof independently reconstructs the inversion-graph toggle lemma: adjacent-position swaps of layered permutations are legal exactly for merging two consecutive singleton layers or splitting a two-element layer. Long layers are therefore fixed, each free gap is the independent-set flip graph of a path and hence a Fibonacci cube, and all component metrics are Hamming distances. Gap-signature enumeration proves the two rational generating functions and a direct edge double count proves the edge formula. An independent deterministic Python checker uses the actual pop-stack operation through n=8, checks all-pairs shortest paths through n=8, and full graph enumerators through n=12. These finite checks supplement rather than substitute for the all-n proof.

originality.rationale: Direct source inspection verifies that the composition representation of one-pass pop-stack sortable permutations is old. The new statement is the precise induced adjacent-position-swap graph decomposition, a result not implied by the permutation count, by iterative pop-stack bounds, or by related reconfiguration results on different avoidance classes. Multiple actual published-finding corpus and web searches for graph/weak-order/alias formulations found no covering statement. This is a best-knowledge originality judgement, not proof of worldwide priority; an unindexed general weak-order result remains a risk.
residual_risks: Historical priority is not certified: an unindexed statement in the theory of induced weak-order graphs or permutation-class adjacency may already imply this exact component theorem.
The Elder–Goh comparison used the accessible abstract only and is not a whole-document NOT_COVERING judgment.
The exact known general Fibonacci-cube structure is standard; originality is claimed only for identifying those components and their signatures in the one-pass pop-stack sortable permutation graph.

value.rationale: Reconfiguration reachability and optimal local editing are natural algorithmic questions for the one-pass sortable permutation class. The result is a complete structural graph isomorphism classification, not an arbitrary slice of a known sequence: it gives all component sizes, diameters, median structure, exact geodesic routing, rational component and isolate counts, and exponential decay of the identity-reachable share. These answer distinct quantities not furnished by the prior sorting and enumeration papers.
